samples.summary: The accepted residual for read-gating `AttachDocument` is documented as "one write" but is unbounded, and it defeats the public-template-tier gate's stated premise, which this change does not reconcile.
samples.evidence: The new Risks text says the residual is "a change pack carried by the attach itself: a hand-rolled client could smuggle one write past that method, while everything after it is refused" (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:292-294; same wording in yorkie-auth.controller.ts:99-102 and packages/backend/README.md:228). But nothing bounds a client to one attach: a share-link *viewer* can build a fresh local Document with one local change, attach (now authorized as a read regardless of verb), detach, and repeat — so the smuggling channel is arbitrarily many writes, not one. That matters beyond this doc because `assertYorkieAuthEnforced` (packages/backend/src/template/template-review.ts:61-97) opens the *public template gallery* on the explicit premise that "unless the auth webhook actually refuses that token's writes" a preview token grants write access, and specifically that "one cheap request per card would empty the gallery into a queue". Read-gating attach re-opens exactly that per-request write path for a non-browser client, yet neither template-review.ts nor the template-gallery design doc is updated to record that its safety argument now rests only on well-behaved clients. Either the residual's characterization should be corrected (repeatable, not single) and the dependent gate revisited, or attach should stay write-gated for viewer-role share identities while remaining read-gated for members.

samples.summary: The e2e spec the design doc now cites as evidence still carries the pre-fix rationale, so the shipped read-gate has no live-server exercise and the comment contradicts the code.
samples.evidence: The design doc cites `packages/backend/test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts` "which omits `AttachDocument` from its registered set for exactly this reason" (docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:279-281). The spec's own comment at lines 371-383 still describes the omission as an unresolved defect — "Gating it as the backend README's own walkthrough suggests would deny a viewer's very first attach outright … See the task report for this as its own follow-up finding" — and line 502 says "`AttachDocument` is not registered above … so this attach is not itself gated". With `READ_GATED_METHODS` shipped, that rationale is stale: the README now instructs registering AttachDocument (packages/backend/README.md:211,222) and the viewer attach would pass. Nothing in the tree exercises the read-gated attach against a real Yorkie server, and the stale comment will mislead the next reader into thinking the gap is still open.

samples.summary: `sideTokenInjector` reimplements the existing `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` helper instead of reusing it, diverging on token lifetime from the two sibling ops scripts.
samples.evidence: `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv(secret?)` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-service-token.ts:75-87) already takes an explicit secret, warns when it is missing, and honors `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN`; its doc comment is written for exactly this use ("for the ops scripts under packages/backend/scripts"). The new local `sideTokenInjector` duplicates the missing-secret warn + injector construction and silently drops the `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN` knob, so `copy-yorkie-documents.ts` now answers "how long is a script's service token good for?" differently from `migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:347` and `migrate-yorkie-cf-ranges.ts:221`, which still call the shared helper. Passing `process.env.SOURCE_JWT_SECRET` into the shared helper (with a per-side message) would keep one implementation.

samples.summary: The new required `SOURCE_JWT_SECRET` / `TARGET_JWT_SECRET` operator contract is recorded only in the script's own `--help`, not in any doc an operator reads before running it.
samples.evidence: The two secrets moved from argv to environment and now have no fallback, so an operator following the recorded invocation in docs/tasks/archive/2026/03/20260314-local-prod-restore-todo.md:77 will get an anonymous attach and a 403 wherever the webhook is registered. Neither packages/backend/README.md's auth-webhook section (lines 198-262) nor docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md (which does document the service-token identity at lines 121-135) mentions the per-side env vars, and docs/design/document-copy.md:100-106 references this script without them.
searchedFor: grep copy-yorkie-documents across docs/ and packages/

samples.summary: User-facing self-hosting guide registers `AttachDocument` without the read-gating explanation the backend README now carries.
samples.evidence: packages/backend/README.md:222-231 explains that AttachDocument is authorized as a read because its verb is always `rw`; the equivalent operator walkthrough in packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:569-582 lists the same method with no such note, so a self-hoster reading only that page will believe attach is write-gated.
